record.browser_session: headless Chrome over the DevTools protocol, viewport 1440 x 900 CSS pixels, device scale factor 1, a fresh profile per session. Input is trusted DevTools input: mouse clicks at an element's centre and held key events on the focused world canvas.

drawn_position_error_millipixels.definition: a reference object placed through the product at each distance mark, captured at a fixed pose relative to it; its silhouette (capture with it minus capture without it) is compared with the same relative capture at the arrival point: centroid shift in thousandths of a pixel, and intersection over union reported beside it
drawn_position_error_millipixels.why: one pixel is the smallest displacement this display can show

frame_work_looking_p95_us.statistic: 95th percentile of per-frame main-thread work over the turns in place
frame_work_looking_p95_us.why: the same display, turning instead of walking

frame_work_walking_p95_us.statistic: 95th percentile of per-frame main-thread work over the walk windows
frame_work_walking_p95_us.why: a 60 Hz display presents a frame every 16.7 ms; work longer than that misses the next presentation and motion stutters

open_complete_world_us.definition: as open_first_frame_us, ending instead at the end of the first drawn frame after every saved object and every placed estimate is resident in the scene
open_complete_world_us.statistic: median over the warm opens, with the cold open reported beside it
open_complete_world_us.why: a first frame without the person's own objects is not their world, so the world they saved gets the same 2 s

open_first_frame_us.definition: (the credential form in the document minus navigation start) plus (the end of the first drawn frame minus the token submit). The operator form is how this runtime authenticates; a signed-in person skips it, so the time the form waits for input is excluded and nothing else is.
open_first_frame_us.statistic: median over the warm opens, with the cold open reported beside it
open_first_frame_us.why: opening a saved world should show it within 2 s on this machine

placement_ack_us.definition: from the trusted click on Confirm to the first animation frame after the objects panel shows the settled report that the object was added
recorded_beside: Place before me click to the verdict reading ready
Confirm click to the new object resident in the scene
placement_ack_us.statistic: median over the placements at a count, with each value listed
placement_ack_us.why: a change a person confirms should visibly land within a quarter second

parts: the authored version read before and after the reload has the same state_sha256 and a byte-equal object list
the scene's resident objects after the reload have the same ids and world positions to 0.1 mm as before it
at the arrival pose, the share of pixels differing by more than 3 levels in any channel is no more than the share between two captures of the same page without a reload, plus 0.1 percentage point
reload_identical.why: reopening a saved world must show the world that was saved

society_reload_p95_us.definition: one society snapshot read plus one read of the latest 256 events
society_reload_p95_us.scope: in-process server cost; HTTP, serialisation and the permission floor excluded
society_reload_p95_us.why: an allocation, not a measurement: a quarter of the 2 s open budget, since the society is one of several reads when a world opens

society_replay_us.scope: in-process server cost; HTTP, serialisation and the permission floor excluded
society_replay_us.statistic: median of the replays at a checkpoint
society_replay_us.why: replay is the verification a person or host can ask for; it gets the open budget

society_tick_p95_us.scope: in-process server cost; HTTP, serialisation and the permission floor excluded
society_tick_p95_us.why: hosted playback runs a tick every 1,000 ms at speed 1 and every 250 ms at speed 4 (exulanica/world/society_controls.py SPEEDS and the 1,000 ms base the control worker uses); a tick longer than the interval falls behind

undo_ack_us.definition: from the trusted click on Confirm for taking back the last change to the first animation frame after the panel shows the settled report that it was taken back
undo_ack_us.statistic: median over the undos at a count, with each value listed
undo_ack_us.why: the same quarter second for taking a change back

builds.debug: the development server the acceptance launcher starts. The playcanvas package resolves to build/playcanvas.dbg through its development export.
builds.debug_comparison: debug is measured once against release on the same world, arrival pose and walk, and the gap is reported as its own result, so a development-server timing can be read against a release one
builds.release: the app built with vite build from the measured commit with VITE_EXULANICA_TOKEN unset, served by vite preview with /api proxied to the isolated API. The playcanvas package resolves to its release build.

declared_limits_of_the_design: Society figures are in-process server cost, not HTTP: serialisation, the permission floor and the network are left out, and a reader must not add them in.
Inhabitants of a saved world are not drawn by the browser at this commit, so no frame cost of inhabitants is measured.
Headless Chrome on one machine. A headed browser with a compositor and a physical display may differ; that is assumed, not measured.
The release build is served by vite preview's proxy, not by a production deployment.
Synthetic photographs, not personal ones; what a real photograph's estimate costs to draw is assumed to scale with its point count, which is recorded.

instrument.application: the engine application object, captured when its constructor registers it under the canvas id, so the scene graph can be read with no debug global
instrument.callback_lag: callback entry time minus the frame timestamp the browser passed
instrument.drawn_frame: a frame whose callbacks issued at least one WebGL draw call, counted by wrapping the draw entry points of WebGL2RenderingContext.prototype
instrument.frame_work: the wall time of every requestAnimationFrame callback from entry to return, measured by wrapping window.requestAnimationFrame. The engine's tick is that callback, so this is the main thread's work for a frame: the engine update, the binding's decisions and render submission. Callbacks sharing one frame timestamp are summed. Frame intervals are recorded beside it and never stand in for it.
instrument.installed_by: a script evaluated before any page script (Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument), so no product file changes
instrument.long_tasks: PerformanceObserver longtask entries over the same window: count and total
instrument.object_residency: additions and removals of scene nodes named authored-object:<id>, timestamped where the engine attaches and detaches them
instrument.pixels: the engine's render followed by gl.readPixels of the default framebuffer in the same task. Never a browser screenshot: the app renders only the frames it wants, so a screenshot can read a stale frame.
instrument.server_timing: request sent to response received for each product request, from the DevTools network events, beside the in-page timings

record.knee: the smallest registered count at which a metric's statistic exceeds its budget, reported as lying between the previous registered count and that one. When the per-run values at a count straddle the budget, the count is reported as at the budget. When no registered count exceeds it, no knee is claimed and the reason the range stops where it does is given.
load_discipline: every browser timing run is wrapped in quiet-slot then gpu-slot, in that order; society timing runs in quiet-slot; builds run in quiet-slot

the one-minute load is read inside the slot before timing starts and again after; a run whose load before exceeds 8 is discarded and retried, three attempts at most, after which the point is recorded as not measured with its loads
the nice value of every measuring process is recorded; zsh background niceness is off
depth estimation never runs inside a timing window

machine.recorded_again: the same facts and the WebGL renderer string are read again with every run

open_questions: Whether frame work reaches its knee inside the registered object range.
Whether anything on the ground surface visibly swims or jitters at 1, 4 or 8 km.
How many photo estimates a world holds before opening or frame work fails, and which fails first.
Whether a reload ever shows a different world from the one saved.
predictions: Placement and undo acknowledgement grow linearly with placed objects: settle awaits redrawAll, which clears every resident object and fetches, hashes, decodes and attaches each one again, one at a time (web/packages/app/src/composition/objects.ts settle, redrawAll, drawEvery; web/packages/atlas-react/src/playcanvas/scene-objects.ts place). Predicted to be the first budget to fail, in both layouts.

Open to first drawn frame does not grow with objects, which are drawn after the renderer mounts (main.ts calls objects.begin after mountRenderer), and does grow with placed estimates, which are fetched and hashed before it mounts (loadAuthoredPointMaps).
Open to complete world grows linearly with objects, for the reason in the first prediction.
The server's apply grows with objects: every edit digests every object (object_repository._append_edit, delta_sha256) and answers with every object and every edit.
Frame work while walking grows with objects in view, one entity and draw per object with no instancing, faster clustered than spread.
Society replay grows with ticks times population, since replay reruns every tick from the first; a tick grows with population.
Drawn position error for an object stays below a pixel at 8 km: float32 spacing at 8,192 m is 0.977 mm, from the endless ground's own measurement.
record.question: How large can a saved world grow through the product's own routes before what a person does in it (opening, reloading, placing and undoing, walking, looking around) stops meeting the budgets below, and which limit does a person meet first?

assumed_rates.society: playback at speed 1, one tick per second

ranking.rule: limits a person meets through the product are ranked by the minutes of ordinary use before they appear; limits no product path reaches at this commit follow them

record.runtime: one isolated API, PostgreSQL 18 server and web server on this machine, a synthetic workspace and bearer token minted per runtime, no model key, no personal photograph. The token is typed into the page's own operator field and held only in page memory.

series.combined: one world holding at once the largest count of each separate series at which every budgeted metric of that series passed (the smallest registered count where none passed), measured once with open, reload, walking and looking

distance.at_each_mark: release the keys, place the reference marker with Place before me, capture the drawn position error, take the placement back, walk on
distance.frame_work: over the whole walk and in the 10 s before each mark
distance.route: from the arrival pose along its facing, holding W and Shift (23.4 m/s, the controls' sprint), in a world with no other object

estimates.made_through: POST /intake, then the personal admission review granting the depth right against the server's exact notice (the same step a person takes), the ingest worker with EXULANICA_DEPTH_MODEL=moge and the cached MoGe-2 checkpoint as the runtime role, then POST /world-entries/{id}/source-attachments and compositions preview and apply as photo_point_map on a 4 m grid in front of the arrival point
estimates.photographs: procedural synthetic room images, distinct per index, no person and no real place

inhabitants.population_note: the product creates 128 for a saved world (SOCIETY_POPULATION); 32, 512 and 2048 are made by overriding that constant inside the measurement process only, which no product path can do
inhabitants.scope: in-process server cost through SocietyRuntime and the society repository
inhabitants.world: a saved starter world on the endless ground with one reviewed marker plate at (3000, 5000) mm, profile exulanica-society/v2

objects.assets: the three reviewed markers in turn by index (cube, pillar, plate)
objects.built_through: POST /world/versions/{id}/compositions/preview then /apply with the runtime's token, the route pair the browser itself uses, one placement at a time
objects.each_layout_in: its own saved world, each in a fresh runtime and workspace

layouts.clustered: a sunflower spiral over a disc of radius 10 m centred 20 m in front of the arrival point along the arrival facing
layouts.spread: a sunflower spiral over a disc of radius 500 m centred on the ground origin

measured_at_each_count: placement and undo through the objects panel (5 pairs)

record.statistics: pooled p50, p95 and maximum per point, and the per-run median and p95 to show the spread between runs; every raw sample is kept beside the record
stop_rules: a budgeted metric that has exceeded its budget at two consecutive registered counts is not measured at larger counts of that series, because its knee is bracketed; the other metrics continue

a series stops growing when every budgeted metric in it has stopped, at its largest registered count, when growing it to the next count through the product routes would take more than 60 minutes at the measured build rate, or when the product refuses to grow it, in which case the refusal is the finding

the estimates series also stops when the placed point maps would exceed 1 GiB in total, or when the page loses its WebGL context or its renderer crashes, in which case the count reached is the finding
the population series stops after two consecutive tick budget failures or when one tick exceeds 60 s; the history series stops when one replay exceeds 600 s
no count, distance or budget in this record is changed after the first timing run; a point added later is reported as added later, with the reason, and cannot be a knee
record.tree_rule: Every figure names the commit it ran on. Before each run the product paths (exulanica/, web/packages/, migrations) are checked unchanged from that commit with git diff --quiet and git status. Measurement drivers live outside the product paths.
unbudgeted_results: the server's preview and apply duration for every placement that builds a world
response bytes of the authored version as it grows

the depth worker's model load wall time, inference wall time per photograph and peak resident memory, run outside every timing window, compared with the figures lane records give for the same checkpoint on this class of machine
society state bytes, events per tick and replay rate in ticks per second

walk_protocol.looking: at the arrival point, hold ArrowLeft for 4654 ms (one full turn at 1.35 rad/s)
walk_protocol.starts_after: the world is complete and 2 s have passed with no input
walk_protocol.walking: from the arrival pose, hold S for 20 s, then hold W for 20 s, heading unchanged, so the arrival view stays in front of the camera throughout; frame work pooled over both windows
